Anyone who receives a distribution or is treated as having a distribution of $10 or more from:

modal-dialog.modal-heading: What if the name on the Form 1099-R is incorrect?

modal-content.p: First, be sure the About you section uses the name that matches your Social Security card or Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN) paperwork.

If the Form 1099-R lists a slightly different name than what was entered in the About you section (for example, it uses an old legal last name or a different middle initial), let the payer know so they can update their records.
However, you don’t need to request a corrected Form 1099-R, and you can continue completing your tax return using the Form 1099-R as it is for the tax year.

modal-dialog.modal-heading: What’s a gross distribution?

modal-content.p: A gross distribution is the total dollar amount a person receives before income tax or other deductions.

modal-dialog.modal-heading: What does taxable amount mean?

modal-content.p: Taxable amount is the part of a gross distribution that is taxable.
The taxable amount is determined by whether the contributions were pre-tax or post-tax and whether the distribution was a rollover.

p.a: Find out more in instructions to Form 1099-R.

If you prefer to calculate the taxable amount yourself, you’ll need to file using another tool.

p.a: Find other ways to file your federal taxes.

modal-dialog.modal-heading: What’s box 6 used for?

modal-content.p: If you received a lump-sum distribution from a qualified plan that includes securities of the employer’s company, the net unrealized appreciation is shown in box 6. Net unrealized appreciation is any increase in value of employer securities while held in the trust.

modal-dialog.modal-heading: What’s the IRA/SEP/SIMPLE box used for?

modal-content.p: The Form 1099-R IRA/SEP/SIMPLE box is checked if a distribution is from a traditional Individual Retirement Arrangement (IRA), Simplified Employee Pension Plan (SEP) IRA, or SIMPLE IRA (Savings Incentive Match Plan for Employees).
The box isn’t checked if a distribution is from a Roth IRA or for an IRA recharacterization.

modal-dialog.modal-heading: What’s box 7 used for?

modal-content.p: Box 7 codes identify the type of distribution you received. There can be up to 2 codes listed that appear as numbers or letters.
Be sure to list all of the codes on your Form 1099-R in Direct File.

modal-dialog.modal-heading: What is a qualified exception to an early distribution?

modal-content.p: Generally, the amounts a person withdraws from a retirement plan before they reach age 59½ are called early or premature distributions. In an early distribution situation, a person must pay an additional 10% early withdrawal tax unless a qualified exception applies. For example, a qualified exception would apply to an early distribution made to a terminally ill employee.

p.a: Learn more about types of qualified exceptions.

modal-dialog.modal-heading: What’s rolling over a distribution?

modal-content.p: Certain payments you receive from a retirement plan or Individual Retirement Arrangement (IRA) can be “rolled over” by depositing the distribution in another retirement plan or IRA within 60 days. When you roll over a distribution, you generally don’t pay tax on it until you withdraw it from the new plan.

If you don’t roll over your payment within 60 days, it will be taxable (other than qualified Roth distributions and any amounts already taxed). You may also be subject to additional tax, unless you’re eligible for one of the exceptions to the 10% additional tax on early distributions.

p.a: Find out more about roll overs.

modal-dialog.modal-heading: What is considered a distribution from a military retirement plan?

modal-content.p: For this question, select Yes if a distribution comes from any military retirement plan, other than the federal Thrift Savings Plan (TSP). For example, types of military retirement plans include:

p.a: Learn more about military retirement plans.

modal-dialog.modal-heading: What is a qualified disaster recovery distribution?

modal-content.p: A qualified disaster recovery distribution is made from an eligible retirement plan to a person whose main home was in a qualified disaster area. This person must have had an economic loss because of the disaster.

p.a: Learn more about qualified disaster recovery distributions.

modal-dialog.modal-heading: Why do we ask if you’re a retired public safety officer?

modal-content.p: A person who is an eligible retired public safety officer can elect to exclude from their taxable income the distributions made from an eligible retirement plan if certain conditions apply:

ul.li: Retirement plan distributions are used to pay the premiums for coverage by an accident or health plan or a long-term care insurance contract
The premiums are for coverage for you, your spouse, or your dependents
The distribution must be from the retirement plan maintained by your employer from which you retired as a public safety officer

p.strong: Who is considered a retired public safety officer?

modal-content.p: A retired public safety officer is someone who’s retired because of disability or because they reached normal retirement age. They must have served at a public agency in an official capacity as a:

p.a: Learn more about the insurance premiums for public safety officers.

modal-dialog.modal-heading: What’s an in-plan Roth rollover (IRR)?

modal-content.p: An IRR is a rollover within a retirement plan to a designated Roth account in the same plan.

401(k), 403(b) and 457(b) governmental plans that have designated Roth accounts may offer IRRs. Plan participants, surviving spouse beneficiaries, and alternate payees who are current or former spouses are eligible to do an IRR in a plan that offers this type of rollover.
Find out more about IRRs.

modal-dialog.modal-heading: What’s the Foreign Account Tax Compliance Act (FATCA)?

modal-content.p: Under the FATCA, foreign banks and other financial institutions report information to the IRS about their U.S. account holders.

If a Form 1099-R has the FATCA filing requirement box checked, it means you hold a foreign account and may need to file one or more additional forms that aren’t supported by Direct File. You need to find another way to file.

modal-dialog.modal-heading: What if there are two amounts listed in box 14?

modal-content.p: In rare tax situations, a Form 1099-R may have two amounts listed in box 14.
If box 14 lists more than one entry for a dollar amount, you’ll need to file your federal taxes using another tool. Find other ways to file your federal taxes.

modal-dialog.modal-heading: What if there are two states listed in box 15?

modal-content.p: In rare tax situations, a Form 1099-R may have two states listed in box 15.
If box 15 lists more than one state, you’ll need to file your federal taxes using another tool. Find other ways to file your federal taxes.

modal-dialog.modal-heading: What if there are multiple entries listed in a box?

modal-content.p: In rare tax situations, a Form 1099-R may have more than one entry in boxes 16-19.
If a box has multiple entries, you’ll need to file your federal taxes using another tool. Find other ways to file your federal taxes.
